SMTO-WEB-0005 — The search service sent back something SMTO can't read

GUID: 65f9cf28-ed60-45c8-b340-46d021a41f0e
Slug: web-provider-response-invalid
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • The search service replied, but its answer was too large or wasn't a list of search results (for example an error page). SMTO didn't use it, so no search results came back.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Capabilities, select Configure Web, and check the provider's Provider type and Base URL match the service, for example your SearXNG server's main address. An address that points to a login page, proxy or a different service returns a web page instead of search results.
  2. Select Test connection for that provider. The test shows whether the service now returns a results list SMTO can read.
  3. If you run SearXNG, ask the person who manages it to make sure it returns search results to other programs and isn't showing an error or block page. SMTO only accepts a reply that contains a list of search results, up to 1 MB.
  4. Meanwhile, choose another enabled provider as Default provider and select Save. Searches can then go to a provider that answers correctly.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Connected, and a new web search returns results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the search service. Don't treat the reply as search results; SMTO discarded it for a reason.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The search provider's successful response could not be used: it exceeded the 1 MiB limit, was not valid JSON, or lacked an object with a results list.

What this means

  • Search response parsing exceeds the one MiB bound, cannot decode JSON, or lacks an object containing a results list. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • Search response parsing exceeds the one MiB bound, cannot decode JSON, or lacks an object containing a results list.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish size rejection, non-JSON response and invalid results structure from an empty valid result set.

How to fix it

  • SearXNGProvider.search in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/providers.py requires a 2xx response of at most 1 MiB that decodes as a JSON object with a results array. Verify the configured base_url targets the provider's search API (not an HTML front end, auth proxy or captive page) and that the provider type matches; then run Test connection.
  • Inspect provider compatibility and safe diagnostics; do not fabricate retrieved content.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The configured provider returns a bounded JSON object with a results list.

What not to do

  • Do not treat an HTML error page or malformed response as valid search results.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
